rationale: The default-promotion decision is to retain strict FP64 and require explicit precision=auto. Source-bound DFT warmup evidence includes five alternating small-water cold/warm/changed E+force pairs that lose to FP64 and four repaired larger cold single-pair screens with FP64/AUTO ratios 0.6385, 0.7430, 0.7159 and 0.8156. Returned repaired endpoints meet their recorded numerical gates and execute mixed J, but neither those screens nor historical HF evidence qualify a general default. Large screens are not repeated promotion trials and their distinct cold guesses prevent attributing every iteration difference to arithmetic. This is a scoped negative default decision, not DFT-MP-v1 completion, a claim about every mixed workload, or a new measurement on current master.
revisit_condition: The narrower precision owners may propose a source-identified guard only after repeatable complete cold/warm/moved endpoint benefit, observed mixed and strict work, all refinement/retry costs and unchanged independent scientific gates. #1189 still requires its frozen per-method 1.20x product result; this negative policy decision does not close or weaken that target.
